items.text: If you need to apply styles manually, you should still follow existing GOV.UK conventions.
For example, do not assign new meanings to colours, do not change the style of buttons or adjust the thickness of borders on form inputs.
Always use the GOV.UK colour palette.
You must make sure that the contrast ratio of text and interactive elements in your service meets Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.2) success criterion 1.4.3 Contrast (minimum) level AA.
Do not copy the specific hexadecimal (hex) colour values.
Only use the variables in the context they’re designed for.
Use this colour for text on dark backgrounds
Only use this colour to indicate which element is focused on.
If you want to reference the spacing scale in your CSS, use the spacing helpers.
items.section: Applying spacing in your own CSS

items.text: For the static spacing scale, use the govuk-spacing function.
Occasionally, you might need to make minor adjustments like adding or removing spacing to elements of your design.
For most types of page, we recommend using either a ‘two-thirds’ or a ‘two-thirds and one-third’ layout.
Never make assumptions about what devices people are using.
The first should have the class govuk-width-container, which sets the maximum width of the content but does not add any vertical margin or padding.
Within govuk-width-container you should add the govuk-main-wrapper class to your <main> element.
Use the grid system to lay out the content on your service’s pages.
Your main content should always be in a two-thirds column even if you’re not using a corresponding one-third column for secondary content.
You can stop elements from being displayed on the page and keep their contents available to screen readers using govuk-visually-hidden.
Check the information the user gives you to make sure it’s valid.
Do not use validation to check whether the user is eligible to use the service or has permission to do something.
items.section: When not to use this pattern

items.text: Use validation to ignore unwanted characters, unless it would make the information too unclear for you to use.
Do not validate when the user moves away from a field.
Wait until they try to move to the next part of the service - usually by clicking the ‘continue’ or ‘submit’ button at the bottom of the page.
Generally speaking, avoid validating the information in a field before the user has finished entering it.
You’ll always need to carry out server side validation, even if you use client side validation.
Only add client side validation if you find a user need for it.
Do not add ‘required’ to your input fields.
